workflow.title: Before cleaning an AI workspace: separate rebuildable files from session history
workflow.primaryIntent: Mac developers deciding what may be rebuilt versus what preserves an AI coding session; not a renamed Mint comparison
workflow.lead: Do not treat an old worktree or agent session as disposable merely because the code is in Git. Classify ownership, active use and rebuild cost before approving changes.
sections: Record the active project and session context without executing cleanup
Read Mint's four buckets as vendor classifications, not a guarantee
Separate build output, caches, worktrees and session history
Review one location and recovery path at a time
Choose file organization/storage optimization or app-activity investigation according to the job
workflow.additionalEvidenceRequired: Any concrete Git/session-loss mechanism or executable procedure needs official tool documentation before drafting; current source only establishes Mint's attributed rationale.
workflow.interactionPass: Hand off a static decision checklist: owner known? in use? reproducible? independent backup? exact proposed action understood? Unknown means stop/review, never auto-delete. No filesystem access or claimed recovered bytes.
workflow.visualPlacement: Mint screenshot after lead only if cleared; Breathing Room Space preview beside the alternate investigation workflow with example-data labels.
